customize.text: Flower-Feather Clan

The
is a tribe located on the cliffs in northern Natlan, living alongside the Qucusaurs. The tribe was founded over two thousand years ago by Lianca, one of the six heroes of Natlan and a companion of the first Pyro Archon. The tribe's settlement is built on a complex network of platforms, walkways, and balloons. The balloons are seen as the wings that lift the Flower-Feather Clan into the skies, and the wooden platforms are considered the "giant claws" that anchor the tribe to the mountains. During the war with the Abyss, Tlalocan's balloons were used to transport people to the battlefield more quickly. The Flower-Feather Clan is one of the proudest tribes in Natlan, and its members often participate in various competitions where they demonstrate their skills.

Members of the Flower-Feather Clan are renowned for their flying squads. The current chief of the tribe, Mutota, was once a true flying ace, and several elders are also members of the elite flying squad. Since ancient times, generation after generation, the elite warriors of the Flower-Feather Clan have protected the tribe, patrolling the skies with their Qucusaurs. Back when Tlalocan was responsible for patrolling and defending all of Natlan, the flying squad was the best of the best — the fiercest warriors in the nation. Clan warriors are proud people, but the Qucusaurs are even prouder. Anyone who wants to become a rider must train tirelessly and then earn the approval of the Qucusaurs, because in the sky, the lives of both depend on the skills of the rider and the connection with the Saurian. To join the elite squad, a special flying test is held, during which one must demonstrate mastery of the relevant skills and earn the approval of the Qucusaurs. Some Saurians are born with wings, just as some people come into this world endowed with innate talent. Others, however, can do nothing else but spend their lives gazing up from the ground. Very few candidates pass this selection, and sometimes, after multiple failed attempts to pass the flying test and win the Qucusaurs' approval, people get so disheartened that they give up on their dream to soar in the skies. They decide to give up trying forever, and in the Clan, such people are called "wingless."

One of the clan members who struggled to pass the flying test for a long time was Coyllur. Although her flying skills were excellent, she was mentally stuck in a rut. First, she failed the test, and then she struggled to summon the Qucusaurs, which further undermined her self-confidence. When the Traveler and Paimon learned of Coyllur, they decided to cheer her up, so the Traveler, possessing a Qucusaurus, flew to the woman's call. She was so overjoyed that she asked the Qucusaurus to practice some of her flying skills, but the hero of the tribe, Chasca, came to the Traveler's aid, calling to the Qucusaurus from afar. Furthermore, the leader of the flying squad and the elder of the clan, Allpa, announced a redo of the flight trials, giving Coyllur a second chance to join the squad.

But not all tribe members were ready to give up and become wingless. Although the elder of the Flower-Feather Clan, Allpa, was the leader of the flying squad, she had become wingless many years ago due to an injury. While wandering across Natlan, she gave birth to a child named Tepal. His birth gave her new hope. She wanted to be a mother who soared through the skies day and night, not a wingless wanderer. But his father wanted to settle down and give the child a safe life within the tribe, so their feelings gradually faded. Tepal's father started a new family in the Children of Echoes tribe and took Tepal for himself, while Allpa returned to Tlalocan alone. The elder hadn't seen her son for many years, but one day he appeared on her doorstep, eager to take the flying test. But when the Qucusaurs rejected him, Allpa felt hurt and angry. Together, they created "phlogiston wings," a flying machine worn on the back. It can be operated using a hand-held trackball, which in turn controls the flow of gaseous phlogiston. Using mechanisms from Ochkanatlan, Tepal built a massive flying laboratory hidden in the clouds. During research, it was discovered that wild Qucusaurs, who possessed the natural ability to process gaseous phlogiston, could be used to create the hand-held trackballs. Tepal didn't want to use the Saurians, but during one of the experiments, unstable gaseous phlogiston exploded, killing a man.

Allpa, wanting to fulfil her son's dream of a sky accessible to all, abandoned all experiments and began using the Qucusaurs. She also sowed seeds of discord within the tribe, so that people would abandon interaction with the Saurians and begin using phlogiston wings. The elder believed that this was the only way the tribe could develop further, and was even prepared to seize the tribe and kill the chief and other elders. As a result of the intervention of the Traveler, Paimon, and Chasca, Allpa was stopped, and many tribe members sided with Mutota and the Qucusaurs, so the rebellion in the Flower-Feather Clan failed. The sky laboratory was dismantled and converted into a sky prison, where Allpa and her followers were imprisoned.

customize.text: Lianca

More than two thousand years ago, the future Natlan was ruled by dragons, including thirteen sovereign rulers. They were artificial intelligences created by the Flamelord, Xiuhcoatl. Among them was the Eighth Lord CL-08 "Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers" Ix Ajkotz'i'j Iq'ismal Waxak, who took in an abandoned human girl and raised her as her own. According to dragon tradition, the matriarch was to give her grown daughter a bow, so she turned to the Second Lord, "Jade Maiden" Ix Je'lal K'ua'l Ka', asking her to forge one for her. At first, the Second Lord refused to fulfill such a humiliating request, even if she were given hundreds of thousands of slaves as a gift. But then she secretly sent a forged weapon with a Source Servant, explaining that the bow was made by a common dragon craftsman in her territory, a shoddy piece made with worthless scrap, and that the Dragonlord herself had nothing to do with it. Ix Je'lal K'ua'l Ka' spoke the truth, for she truly did not forge "crude weapons for those insignificant humans." She inlaid the bow with jade stones, which she carefully preserved for centuries. When Lianca came of age, the Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers presented her with the weapon and blessed her for her journey. In addition to the bow, the Eighth Lord left her daughter a Moon Wheel, an ancient artifact through which the Three Moons communicated with their followers many millennia ago.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Lianca, my dearest and beloved daughter, my pride and joy"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Go, and find your own path, like your brothers and sisters"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Though you have neither hard scales, nor claws and fangs as sharp as razors"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Remember that you will always be the daughter of the mother of dragons, an honorable princess"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"In this world, you kneel to no one, be they human or dragon"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Choose your path with pride, just like a true dragon"</color>

Lianca set out to find her way and visited many lands, both human and dragon. She realized that the world was wide and vast, but only birds could soar through it freely and unrestrained. Laws held mortals in thrall, while obsession confined dragonkind. So-called "freedom" was an article of faith for the strong alone. So she decided to break all chains and shackles that hold the weak back from flight, and be shot from the sky. At first, only a few orphans who had nowhere to go joined her, then wandering warriors, unwilling to be bound by the rules of the tribe, followed her song, and then those dragons who had been banished also came to the forest, seeking her protection. The uncrowned princess accepted them all, human or dragon, whether they had been foe or friend before: she defeated a bandit massive as a mountain who would waylay passersby, and then, all former enmity forgotten with a hearty laugh. The evil, arrogant dragon was shot down three times and cured three times, and they became fast friends. This was the founding moment of the tribe that would be known as the "Flower-Feather Clan" for the next thousand years. A clan where even those who were weak, feeble, and homeless would no longer need to fear the wind and open sky.
On her journey, Lianca met an outlander hailed as
who invited her to join him. She was not the queen of her clan, for all the people around her were free and subservient to no one. But Lianca shared Xbalanque's aspirations, so she followed him and his best friend, Och-Kan, becoming one of the six heroes of Natlan.

<color=#ffffffd9>"However, if you are as sincere as your words, if you truly desire to whip up a blazing wind to burn away the eternal shackles"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"If you truly wish to bestow the weak with a place where they are equal, then, O Outlander, whom they acclaim as a hero, I shall journey with you."</color>

When Lianca joined Xbalanque and stood against the ancient dragons, the Dragonlords accused her mother of treason and demanded her execution. The Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers was proud of her daughter and the path she had chosen. If the other dragons could not defeat her, it was their fault. By decision of the court of sovereign rulers, the Eighth Lord was executed, but almost all of them were later defeated by Lianca, Xbalanque, and his companions in the war against the dragons. Afterward, Xbalanque was reborn from the Sacred Flame, becoming the first Pyro Archon and receiving his first Ancient Name. Later, Lianca received the Ancient Name
After defeating the dragons, Lianca became the First Speaker of the Flower-Feather Clan, the proudest tribe in Natlan.

When Xbalanque entered the Sacred Flame, he left the rule of Natlan to his best friend, Och-Kan. The latter despised everything associated with dragons and persecuted anyone who showed even the slightest sympathy for their civilization. The surviving dragons and their descendants were forced into hiding. Among them was the Eleventh Dragonlord, "Mirror of the Dawning Morn," the proudest of all the sovereign rulers and the most hostile toward humanity. When the Pyro Sovereign fell, she could not accept the dragons' defeat and plunged into utter despair and madness. Deprived of her territory, she was tormented by the question of whether to strike back at humanity and exact revenge or search for a new home. In the end, her mind split into two parts: one, the sovereign ruler who swore revenge against humanity; the other, a malfunction, who longed to seek a new home. The sovereign ruler approached Lianca and Ixquieh, the founder of the Children of Echoes tribe, to trick them into destroying the "malfunction," but they saw through her. Lianca turned the Eleventh Lord's plan against her, sealing her within a dragon prison her mother designed. Ixquieh implanted the Moon Wheel into the core of the "malfunction." They sent the latter on its journey, hoping that even after a thousand years, it would find a home.

During his reign, Och-Kan attempted to rid himself not only of the dragon descendants but also of those who did not support him. The proud Lianca, a former friend of Och-Kan, refused to aid the Grand Alliance but had no intention of fighting him, as they owed each other more than their lives. The First Speaker pitied him, as he did not know whether he was a human or a dragon. The more he chased the sun, the more it blinded him to the creatures who live by its light. Even when Lianca's own son suggested that the tyrant of the Forbidden City get rid of the First Speaker, she considered Och-Kan her friend, not her enemy, to the end.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Heh... Old friend, you need only take care of little old me. Why the need to dispatch hundreds of men?"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Still, as it was I who misjudged my own blood... Then allow me to repay the blood-debt with blood."</color>

Lianca stood straight and tall amidst the overflowing crimson river and fought to the last. The very first arrow fell to her treacherous heir, the rest to the tyrant's minions. Her bones were shattered, and her strength was ebbing from the heroine who had shot countless dragons in the skies. So with her last arrow, she nailed her shattered body to the jade bow, lest death force the proud daughter of dragons to bend her knee.

<color=#ffffffd9>"My honored mother... Your daughter has finally found her own path"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Only suffering belongs to me, and only my song belongs to me... Let this be my epitaph"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"To remember the pain I endured... and finally, surmounted."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"I once offered my life to all, and now... I offer my death to the world."</color>

After the death of Lianca and her son, Lianca's youngest daughter took over the Flower-Feather Clan. For a long time, she hunted the giant dragon, which decades earlier the First Speaker had pierced through the throat with an arrow and forced into the deep forests, depriving the dragon of the simple pleasure of ravaging human villages. The dragon believed that Lianca's daughter was only a frail echo of her mother, powerless against its sharp claws, much less her ghastly, fearful fate. The dragon could be seduced with words, so certain of its mastery of fate, it was convinced it could resist the inevitable conclusion that awaited. Lianca's daughter lured the dragon into a narrow cave through deception, but the dragon refused to admit he had fallen for the trick. It was in this moment that the dragon caught the faintest whiff of a strange smell lingering in the air, and for a brief moment, the dragon felt uneasy, but it quickly vanished under the weight of arrogance. By the time it realized the danger, it was too late. The containers of liquid phlogiston shattered, and a gushing rain of fire consumed its flesh. Thick black smoke began to rise, suffocating the few remaining dim slivers of light that crept through the crevices in the stone walls, as if it were trying to devour the faint sun of the autumn twilight. The woman's hand fell, and the feathered arrow shot through the chill of the autumn's evening air, careering towards the giant dragon that writhed in agony among the flames below.

As a child, Lianca's youngest daughter had a friend who, many years later, became a Recording Officer of the Grand Alliance. On Och-Kan's orders, he came to the Flower-Feather Clan to receive the banner of the tribe and marry the Speaker, believing she lacked the strength to rule the tribe. Only he, who had accompanied that daughter since their youth and was deeply trusted by the tyrant of the Forbidden City, was worthy of leading these ignorant people toward the future that Och-Kan had described. The officer saw in Lianca's daughter only the complete opposite of her mother: quiet and compliant, never one to resist, and accepting without question all that fate had in store for her. Together, they entered the warehouse to retrieve the banner, where he caught the faintest whiff of a strange smell, like oil, or perhaps dry wood, but he paid it no mind. The officer told himself that he would guide the Speaker forward, just as he would one day lead the entire Tlalocan. When he raised his head, he saw the skull of a giant dragon above. As soon as they turned the corner and saw the Flower-Feather Clan banner, flames slid between the woman's fingers. Within a moment, a great conflagration began to roar up on all sides, engulfing the entire warehouse, the narrow space transforming instantly into a blazing crematorium. The officer grabbed her hand in fear, trying to escape the falling flames, but she quietly replied, <color=#ffffffd9>"There's no way out. I've sealed off all the exits."</color> Black smoke stifled her breath, but she summoned her last strength, crawled toward the officer, and clumsily reached out to cradle his face and give him one final farewell kiss. <color=#ffffffd9>"Not even death can part us,"</color> she whispered, attempting to raise a hand that had now lost all feeling. Through the searing tongues of fire, which at this point had nearly obscured the light of the dusk, she saw a group of people hurrying toward them. She smiled and looked up at the dragon's head, imagining the scene that would ensue when the flames were extinguished, picturing the expressions on the people's faces. When the clan members extinguished the fire, they saw two charred bodies and the dragon skull that hung high above them — a relic of the beast that she, singlehandedly, had slain some years past.

customize.text: The Fall of Ochkanatlan

Lianca wasn't the only one who opposed the Grand Alliance. After her death, the elder of the Flower-Feather Clan, who only ostensibly obeyed Och-Kan, banished a scarlet-eyed young man from the tribe, so he would escape the tyrant's capture for defending the Saurians. Thus did this hero, valiant as a bird of prey, embark on a pilgrimage from that night on. His scarlet eyes burned like the sun in the gloom as they reflected only the cold, aqua-colored moon ring that hung high up in the sky above. During Och-Kan's reign, a decree was given that none should ever again give ear to the instructions left by the deep messengers of twilight, the distant ancestors, and the first ascended, to hear them not from the mud-caked roots of trees, the flickering flames of bonfires, or the reflections found in the deep woods. The red-eyed youth, through countless calamities, returned from the kingdom where water flowed as rays of light to the hilly heights of the Forbidden City. As he stepped into the floating garden, the raspy warning of the blind, stooped old woman still clutched at his ear:

<color=#ffffffd9>"As radiant flowers still blossom amongst the clinging vines of distant marsh,</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Go seek, for here is the land of death, piled high with the skulls of behemoths—</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Go seek those the truly righteous, who are still willing to stand in the cold, cruel night, to throw themselves onto the fire,</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>And remember — never betray their passion, their hatred, their greed, and their ambition!</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Do not break faith with the eyes of those still willing to gaze upon the burning flames."</color>

The first to join the scarlet-eyed youth was Sakkuk, a daughter of the mines from the Children of Echoes. Next came the heroic twins Atawallpa and Waskar: the elder, whose teeth were sharper than any blade, and the younger, whose back still bore the marks of the tyrant's whip. Upon hearing of how the scarlet-eyed youth had saved the Saurians, the ordnance officer of the Grand Alliance, Yupanqui, who did not dare to rebel against his old friend, decided to contribute his strength. To get into the Forbidden City, they needed a man who knew all the roads, paths, and secret passages of the city and could operate any mechanisms. And then the silent Yupanqui named the master Manqu.

Manqu had once been a master in the Grand Alliance and worked on the excavations of ancient dragon ruins. Due to the Abyss's infestation, Och-Kan ordered the excavation site sealed and the taint burned away, but many workers were burned alive. Manqu managed to escape alive, but he was forced to spend his time in filthy taverns until he encountered Sakkuk, who was searching for the craftsman who had created a masterful turquoise feather for her father. The scars of having been burnt by a raging blaze marred the half of his face that was hidden under a hat, the flesh a melted slurry of blood, but Sakkuk was not afraid and handed him the plume. When he learned that the man to whom he gave the feather was the girl's father, the craftsman agreed to serve her master. In his heart, he was actually willing to serve her, as well, but he saw that by that time, the scarlet-eyed youth had already occupied the girl's heart. Later, during the overthrow of the ruler of the Grand Alliance, the craftsman Manqu was unable to escape from the burning city, as the Flower-Feather Clan had sealed the secret exits.

The scarlet-eyed youth, guided through numerous trials, was able to defeat the tyrant of the Forbidden City. Och-Kan believed that Xbalanque, whom he loved and for whom he shed golden tears, should be left without a successor, so there was no Archon during his reign. The scarlet-eyed youth summoned the god's fiery wrath, burnt the corroded city to ash, and restored the tribe to its own. To emulate Xbalanque, the first human to ascend, he was to sacrifice his heart with a golden dagger. Self-sacrifice was seen as an honor reserved for the victor — and thus, without even a moment's hesitation, he sliced open his chest with the gleaming blade. And when he returned from the kingdom where water flows as rays of light, he became the second Pyro Archon of Natlan. He believed that people should not place their faith in so-called noble names or offer futile prayers to anyone but themselves. So that people would know that every human could become a god who guides people, the scarlet-eyed youth asked Sakkuk, who was in love with him, to erase his name from history. And although Sakkuk considered him and Master Manqu, whose name had also been erased from history, selfish, she carried out his command.

<color=#ffffffd9>"You will not take me with you to the Flame... And you will not even allow my name to stand alongside yours in history...</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>...Such selfishness. You are also selfish. And he is no better.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Hm... If so, I too will be greedy, ■■■■■.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>The feather you left me will be passed down from generation to generation for a thousand years in your homeland, to which you never returned."</color>

The scarlet-eyed youth, whom Sakkuk loved so much, fulfilled his mission and returned to the Sacred Flame, leaving behind nothing but a warm glow. Centuries later, the story of the scarlet-eyed savior became surrounded by legends. Poems born of fiction were as numerous as stars in the sky, and over the long centuries, their plots intertwined, and debates about the hero's adventures never ceased. The descendants of the Children of Echoes believed that the holy bird was moved by his noble ideals, and gave of its flesh and blood to make this keenest of bows. With its feathers, it directed the blessed hero and led him to their noble ancestor, Sakkuk. Others believed that the scarlet-eyed hero would not aimlessly follow the songs of forest birds. In their legends, the scarlet-eyed youth was never a mere mortal, but rather a thread of thought that came from the One Entombed With the Primal Fire, returning from the Night Realm to save the oppressed. The waters of the People of the Springs were polluted, and the land of the Children of Echoes was covered with dangerous mud. Black winds ravaged the lands of the Flower-Feather Clan, and the already specific and fragile Ley Lines of Natlan were completely devastated. At first, the Natlanese believed that destruction was the Abyss's primary instinct, but its methods began to confirm its intelligence. Each disaster seemed to be specially "designed" for a specific tribe.
The first to rise against the disaster was Tenoch, exiled from his tribe and stripped of his Ancient Name. He was joined by six heroes of Natlan, bearing the Ancient Names of the companions of the first Pyro Archon. Among them was Menilek, a brave warrior from Tlalocan, bearing the Ancient Name

customize.text: Jade of Return

Ten years after the end of the Cataclysm, a legend arose in Natlan about the Jade of Return, a secret treasure capable of repelling the Abyss and banishing it from the world once and for all. It was akin to a golden wheel that could reverse time's flow, burning away the writhing agonizing present and bringing the beautiful past back. And this treasure could only be obtained in the depths of Ochkanatlan, flooded with filth. People, desperate to fight the Abyss, decided to try their luck and search for the Jade, even if it meant a trap. When Natlan was overrun by corruption, an evil dragon appeared in the Forbidden City. All the adventurers who went in hopes of destroying the Abyss were defeated by the dragon, and almost none of them returned.
Among these adventurers was a group that set out for the skyship "Tonatiuh," built by the tyrant of the Forbidden City. The most powerful warrior of the Flower-Feather Clan, Taika, became the squad's leader. In his youth, he had been a follower of the great warrior Fietena, who hailed from the Collective of Plenty but lived with her husband in Tlalocan. Although she lacked the Ancient Name, when Natlan faced the black wave, she donned the hero's mask and became a great warrior. When the disaster finally subsided, the aged Fietena removed the mask that had helped her play the hero for so many years and gave it to young Taika.

<color=#ffffffd9>"It seems this was my final battle... Come now, no need to look so grim."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"When the storm passes, a rainbow will shine; but remember, its false colors are but illusions in the mist."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Whether truly a hero or just acting the part, there will always come a day when it's your turn to bow out."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"That is the way of the wrestler. But now, Taika, let this mask bear witness to the journey before you."</color>

The tribe built atop the mountains would regularly host combat tournaments, in which contestants would wear special masks. These served to intimidate opponents, but contestants also saw them as symbols for themselves. Whenever a masked warrior took the field, their fans would roar out, yet fall silent when the opposition made their entrance. But when the man wearing the feather mask bearing a falcon's semblance entered, all would be strangely silent. Before the Cataclysm, Taika was the mightiest warrior in the Flower-Feather Clan, always getting the upper hand during these rites of contention. Sometimes he grew bored, thinking that this was how his entire life would be. Only after witnessing true war did Taika feel the full weight of destiny. He said goodbye to his wife and unborn child and became a fearsome demon on the battlefield to vanquish demons and monsters. In the Forbidden City, he discovered the blueprints of Ochkanatlan, thanks to which the group was able to find the Altar of Primal Fire and reach the flying ship. But the battle on the Tonatiuh was his last, and as he fell in a pool of blood at the top of the Forbidden City, countless scenes flashed before his eyes. He saw the crimson flame of the ancient land bloom before him once again, like a field ablaze with flowers. He glimpsed the fiery red flames of the ancient land bloom before them once more, like fields of flowers upon the plains. <color=#ffffffd9>"The gates of hell are stained red by the flowing blood of the brave. Let me offer my blood, and leave the key to those gates with my child."</color> Or perhaps what he saw was the faint light through the crack in that gate, at the last reminding him of the words he said to his beloved wife as they parted.
<color=#ffffffd9>"...If it's a girl, call her Bona. She will surely become an outstanding warrior."</color>

Another member of Taika's party was the warrior Quenin of the Flower-Feather Clan. Every night during their expedition, as he tried to sleep, he heard the voices of monsters in the Forbidden City, which were capable of disguising themselves in different forms. They hid in the ancient ruins, keeping him awake. When the pitch-black tide almost reached the team, Quenin stayed to evacuate the survivors so that the rescue team from the Flower-Feather Clan could take them to a safe place. Sometimes, he woke up and saw that a road that was perfectly intact just the day before had now become broken and dilapidated, and sometimes, he saw friends who were long gone. Quenin fell in battle with these monsters, and his form was taken by one of them. Not realizing that he had been a monster himself, Quenin continued to protect adventurers. Only when the Traveler revealed the secret of the fallen warrior did he realize that he had long since become a monster.

When Taika's daughter, an adventurer named Bona, grew up, she decided to continue her father's work and secretly journeyed to the Forbidden City to retrieve the Jade of Return. While fleeing from the evil dragon, she discovered the Core of Chu'ulel, which was once the heart of the entire city. Using the Pyrophosphorite left to her by her father, the adventurer awakened the dragon spirit dormant within the mechanism and named it Cocouik. Using the clues left by Taika's group, Bona and Cocouik reached the Altar of the Primal Fire, from which the Tonatiuh could be ascended. With Cocouik's help, the girl finally understood the true nature of the Jade of Return: there was no treasure that could destroy the Abyss, and the Jade was just a legend concocted by the Sage of the Stolen Flame to lure adventurers. The
was a mechanism capable of saving Natlan but destroying humanity. Realizing the Sage's plan, Bona vowed to prevent the Golden Entreaty and the last Pyrophosphorite from the Sage of the Stolen Flame and not allow his plan to come to fruition. She stopped him, but at the cost of her life, and even Cocouik couldn't save her

More than four hundred years later, the Traveler, Paimon, and their Tepetlisaurus companion arrived in the Forbidden City. They were attacked by an evil dragon and the Abyssal monsters, but were saved by a mysterious golden glow that locked the door of the tower and separated them from the monsters. In the tower, they discovered the notes of the adventurer Bona, which she left behind during her journey to the Forbidden City, and soon they met Bona herself, who remained in the city as a ghost, and Cocouik, who saved them from monsters. Neither Bona nor the Traveler knew that the girl was dead, so they decided to join forces and search for the Jade of Return. When they reached Tonatiuh together and retrieved the Jade of Return, Bona suddenly remembered that she had already been on the skyship and was about to destroy the Jade of Return so that it would not fall into the hands of the Sage of the Stolen Flame. The girl remembered her death and the trap left at the Golden Entreaty. Suddenly, the evil dragon appeared in the sky, snatched the Golden Entreaty, and flew away. After a chase, it turned out that the evil dragon was the body of Och-Kan, infected by the Abyss.
was finally able to reunite with his body and shared the memories with the Traveler of meeting the adventurers, his journey with Bona, and the plan of the Sage of the Stolen Flame. When the Traveler and Paimon returned to the Tonatiuh, Bona had already disappeared, and all that was left of her were her goggles. Although she was unable to complete the story in life, she sacrificed herself to prevent the Sage of the Stolen Flame from obtaining the Golden Entreaty. Bona dreamed of becoming a great adventurer, and the Traveler and Paimon promised to tell everyone about her fate and what happened on the Tonatiuh.

customize.text: The War with the Abyss

The Abyss is the oldest enemy of the Natlan, and every tribe has the memory of its influence. Orphans of the war with the Abyss were not uncommon, and one of them was Chasca, the future hero of Natlan. As a child, she was infected by the Abyss, and it continued to live within her, fueling aggression and conflict. When she was adopted by a family from the Flower-Feather Clan, the shaman told them: <color=#ffffffd9>"The Abyss has a foothold in her soul, and its claws have engraved conflict into her. This wound can only grow worse with the passing years... This is an ominous sign, and something that we have never before seen. ...Perhaps it might be best for all if we took this chance to return her to the forest now."</color> The Abyss has always been Natlan's sworn enemy, and keeping it within the tribe meant bringing disaster. Chasca's adoptive father, Cusco, knew that "return to the mountains" was but a euphemism for "abandoning her to her fate," but he wasn't ready to part with her. Chasca's desire to fight was as natural to her as the desire to eat, but her thirst was like a bottomless hunger. Even the sweet food of constant victory could only satiate her temporarily. Cusco knew that if this thirst couldn't be contained, she would inevitably destroy everything around her or perish in a brutal battle, but he chose to keep Chasca in the hope that she would overcome the Abyss within herself.

Many clan members feared that Chasca's "sickness" was contagious, so they didn't allow their children to play with her younger sister, Chuychu, and treated Cusco and his family poorly. They constantly insulted Chasca, and she would fight them, which only escalated the conflict. The girl often ran away from home and felt she didn't belong in the tribe. Since childhood, she'd heard a voice inside her, which at first had merely guided her to hunt, to bite into her prey, but then it came more frequently, and its noise made her dizzy. Chasca would faint, and release only came when she gave in and created chaos. When she saw people arguing, the voice of the Abyss became clearer and more enticing. One day, she fled into the forest again after a fight with her sister and other children, and the voice inside screamed in her head at her to break everything that hurt her, to tear apart everything that stood in her way. Chasca began to pound on a tree, as if she could tear out this voice and smash it to pieces, but "it" laughed even more wildly. And when her fists were a mess of split skin and muddied flesh, exposing the white bone beneath in some spots, the voice in her head faded. None of Chasca's family knew where she had gone, so she prepared herself to die among the trees, and that was fine to her. When she woke up, her younger sister, Chuychu, was sitting before her, building a fire and bandaging her hands. She called Chasca home, and Chasca agreed, muttering a word she had just learned.

One day, after people complained about Chasca and the beatings, the tribe's elder and captain of the flying squad, Allpa, took it upon herself to teach her. But no matter how hard Allpa labored to explain the human world and its laws, little Chasca couldn't understand what was wrong with fighting. And while Allpa spoke and gestured, Chasca studied her, wondering if she could avoid the lectures by simply defeating the elder. But when Allpa came a second time to teach Chasca, she immediately saw something change in the girl's gaze. Chasca asked to be taught so that she could become strong and defeat the Abyss. And then Allpa decided to teach her how to use humanity's greatest weapon — the language. At first, the girl couldn't understand how this would help her win, but she knew she couldn't tear that voice from her heart and beat it until it was silent. So she endured, learning every last word that Allpa taught her, chewing on that woven scroll that she never thought she would read, bit by bit, line by line. Over time, Chasca became a peacemaker, called upon to mediate disputes and conflicts. And although she can now resolve conflicts with words, in extreme cases, she still resorts to her power.

Even after becoming a peacemaker, resolving any disputes between humans, Saurians, and tribes, Chasca couldn't resolve the conflict with the Abyss. Ever since she learned to live with "it" living within her, "its" voice grew ever weaker, and for a time, Chasca even thought "it" had disappeared. But during the Night Warden War, "it" was invigorated by the Abyss, and like a butterfly bursting from a chrysalis, it manifested as an illusion — one identical to her. <color=#ffffffd9>"We meet at last. Long have we fought, with neither of us able to overcome the other... But come, let us end this. Approach me, embrace me... and the greatest strength shall be yours."</color> As the battle wore on, the more monsters Chasca slew, the greater the hold the Abyssal power had over her, and once more, she felt her battle lust growing ever greater. On that horrific battlefield, the illusion with its outstretched hand seemed almost like an envoy bringing peace. But instinct brought Chasca's gun up and level with it. More phantasms emerged and rushed her, bringing the feelings she'd kept buried back into the open. She remembered how everyone had rejected her, how no one could extinguish the fire within her. She walked forward, step by step, and the power of the Abyss enshrouded her. Chasca shivered and grew faint, but the feeling was familiar, like that of an infant returning to their mother's embrace. But just as she was about to touch the illusion, she heard the voices of her family, supporting her. Raising her gun once more, she took aim and let fly with all the bullets she had in it. The phantom shattered like a mirror when struck, red ichor seeping between the shards. <color=#ffffffd9>"Hah, you hypocrite... You say you wish to stop fights, and yet you raise your gun to me. How pathetic."</color> The illusion vanished like smoke, leaving only a hollow voice that rang in her ears. <color=#ffffffd9>"No. I know 'you' too well. That's why I'm sure that this is the only way to make peace between us."</color> And as she was about to reload, she saw the Vision appear, helping her defeat the voice.

The last time the Abyss within Chasca erupted was during the Abyss's attack on Natlan. Abyss monsters simultaneously attacked all the tribes and the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. Soon, the entire clan territory was contaminated by the Abyss, and Chasca and Chuychu were near the stadium. They were attacked by monsters, and although the attack was repelled, Chuychu was seriously injured. Even when her body was cleansed of the Abyss, it was too late.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Chasca... I used to think mom and dad were crazy for adopting you...</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>I was the younger sibling, but I always felt like it was my job to help mom and dad take care of you... I thought I could set you free from the Abyssal energy you struggled with...</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>I just didn't want anything to happen to you, or to anyone else because of you...</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>I worried about you so much. But now, I realize... I never really understood what it's like for you.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>The fact that you survived an Abyssal contamination was a miracle, but it also left you in a constant state of agitation...</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>The fact that we became family was another miracle. But with me worrying about you all the time, it feels like I just agitated you even further.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>All you ever did was love me, same goes for mom and dad. I've always known that, and I feel terrible, because I really did want to get along as a family.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>No need to apologize. You didn't do anything wrong — no one did. It's nobody's fault that things didn't turn out great.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>I get it now. So, no nagging from me this time.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>...You keep forging ahead, Sis.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Never slow down, and never hold back. Spread your wings and fly free, like the fiercest qucusaur in the sky. Show the world who the bravest Flower-Feather warrior is...</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Because that's who you are... and that's the sister I'm proud of."</color>

The loss of her sister awakened the Abyss energy within Chasca, dormant since her childhood injury, but she was able to bend it to her will. The pain Chasca felt at the loss of Chuychu had awakened her Ancient Name, Vuka, and her ancestor Menilek, who bore the same Ancient Name five hundred years ago, recognized her as the sixth and final hero of Natlan

<color=#ffffffd9>"How unfair life can be... She's had the odds stacked against her from the very beginning, and each step forward has been an agonizing one. Maybe she would have been better off embracing her pain...</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>But her journey goes on, and one question looms large in her mind: If she could rise above the layers of pain, and ascend over the dark clouds of her mind... what, then, would she find?</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Maybe the glorious light of the sun, or maybe a dark, empty Abyss. There is only one way to find out. She needs to spread her wings and soar to new heights... that is the true meaning of life.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>'My life's suffering shall be my epitaph.'</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>'To remember the pain I endured…'</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>'...And, finally, transcended.'"</color>

Returning with Chuychu to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Chasca asked for her body to be cared for and went to the Pyro Archon to fulfill her sister's hopes and sacrifice. Once all six heroes necessary for Mavuika's plan were recognized by their Ancient Names, she used their power and the power of the divine throne to banish the Abyss.

But even after the war with the Abyss was over, many could not recover from the event. Some warriors of the tribe were struck by sudden and powerful Abyssal energy, damaging not only their bodies but also their minds. This illness was called Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome. Those affected began to hallucinate as if the Abyss were chasing them, and that the people around them were monsters. This mental suffering was linked to repressed fears and anxieties. One of the warriors, Atoco, believed he was in cold water while the Abyss was catching up with him, calling for his Saurian companion, who had died four years earlier during an Abyss attack. To help the victim, the Traveler lit a fire for him and brought him a Qucusaurus resembling the warrior's companion. Realizing it wasn't his companion, the warrior awoke from his hallucinations.

Another victim, Cochitta, was about twelve years old when her parents were killed by Abyss monsters before her eyes, leaving her and her younger brother alone. Afterward, Cochitta trained diligently, but was too weak to fight. Until one day, the monsters burst into her and her brother's home. When guards arrived, they found Cochitta standing with a weapon in her trembling hands, her brother hiding behind her. The defeated monster lay at her feet, but she didn't even look at it, and just kept repeating the same thing over and over — <color=#ffffffd9>"you're the only family I have left. I won't let anything happen to you."</color> And from then on, she changed dramatically. She began participating in all the battles against the Abyss and gradually earned a reputation as a brave warrior. Everyone in the tribe thought she had finally overcome her fear, but Cochitta had only buried it deeper, and a powerful blast of Abyssal energy unleashed it once again. To help the warrior, she was allowed to fight the monsters of the Abyss, and she awoke from her hallucinations, realizing the Abyss wasn't so terrifying.

The third victim, the warrior Ocotlan, believed the tribesmen around him were monsters of the Abyss, and even saw his father as nothing more than a monster. Ocotlan was a brave and determined warrior, ready to fight to the last, and so he could not be shaken from his hallucinations. The only solution was to use the Draught of Lucidity, a kind of medicine that can dispel the psychological impact of the Abyss. This elixir was invented by a military doctor from Khaenri'ah, Guthred, five hundred years ago. The treatment had serious side effects, such as lifelong migraines, so it was only used in the most extreme cases. Thanks to the elixir, Ocotlan awoke from his hallucinations and was able to recognize his father.

customize.text: Bloomflower Trials

Several centuries ago, the Bloomflower Trials were held in Natlan — a competition to obtain Sacred Flame Crystals. The Pilgrimage produced enough Sacred Flame, and the Bloomflower Trials became unnecessary, so over time, all memory of them faded. At the time of the last Bloomflower Trials, the tribes were divided and constantly at odds with each other. The Saurian companion of the Flower-Feather Clan doctor, Nampol, fell ill from consuming too much phlogiston, and Nampol was determined to find a way to save him. Antu, the Qucusaurus, was dear to Nampol, and he promised to stand by his side until he grew to adulthood and spread his wings. Nampol studied the scrolls and learned that Ocean Zephyr and Sacred Flame Crystals could help Antu. Sacred Flame Crystals emerged as a result of intertribal conflicts, and when tribes remained united, they would periodically hold the Bloomflower Trials to obtain the Crystals. Research on the Sacred Flame Crystals was incomplete, so no definitive conclusions were reached, but people learned that they could be used to treat certain chronic phlogiston-related illnesses. Others believed the crystals could make warriors stronger. Nampol asked the chiefs of all the tribes to send people to participate in a simplified version of the Bloomflower Trials, and they agreed, despite the tense relations between the tribes, as the doctor treated patients from all tribes. He entrusted his brother, Imaru, the Flower-Feather Clan's chief, with conducting the competition, while he himself set out to search Ocean Zephyrs for Antu.

In Nampol's absence, the Flower-Feather Clan became intrigued by the Sacred Flame Crystals' special powers. Instead of competing fairly, they reignited the feud between tribes, engaging in bloody warfare to seize as many Crystals as possible. Antu, who witnessed their conflicts, decided that the Sacred Flame Crystals were beguiling the hearts of people, so he left the tribe. When Nampol returned with the Ocean Zephyrs, Imara had already spent all the Crystals on research, considering the clan's needs more important than Antu's life. Nampol left the tribe and sought out his companion to spend the rest of his life with him. He begged the leaders of the other tribes to give him some Sacred Flame Crystals, but they all refused. One of the members of the Children of Echoes once showed them a Crystal to show off, then quickly put it away. At that moment, Antu threw himself at the crystal and, with the last of his strength, tried to destroy it, believing that they were the cause of the feud. In the young Saurian's mind, the only reason they began collecting the Sacred Flame Crystals was to save his life. <color=#ffffffd9>"If I hadn't been there, none of this would have ever happened."</color> He watched these once cheerful people turn from best friends to bitter enemies, and he concluded that the Sacred Flame Crystals must have corrupted them. Before his death, Antu was overcome with an all-consuming sadness and guilt, and Nampol himself lived his entire life with this feeling. If he had participated in the competition himself and seen the greed in his brother's eyes, he could have saved Antu. Nampol immersed himself in the study of medicine and spent his life healing the Saurians. He buried his companion on a hill near the tribe and recorded everything about the last Bloomflower Trials on scrolls, hoping that many years from now, the people would learn from their mistakes.

Nampol's descendants continued his work and excelled in vet science. The last of their generation was Ifa, the best Sauro-vet of the Flower-Feather Clan and all of Natlan. As a child, he learned that few of his kind practiced the profession despite their knowledge, so he decided he would not become a vet. Although Ifa had studied medical books since childhood, the words and diagrams drifted through his mind like a breeze. He soon began to understand the contents of the books, but still had no intention of becoming a vet. When his parents died due to the influence of the Abyss, seventeen-year-old Ifa felt a sense of emptiness and didn't know what he wanted in life. He eventually became a vet and soon became known as the Sauro-vet with the finest skills, the gentlest temper, and the strongest sense of responsibility. Once his heart was set, his mind dwelled on other matters no longer. And as the war raged ever fiercer, his list of tasks only grew, but it was this very burden of work that helped him through a difficult period of his life. And when the war with the Abyss ended, and he finally had time to reflect on his life, he realized that everyone has their own tasks, and he simply wanted everyone to be happy.

When Antu died several centuries ago, his soul did not return to the Night Kingdom but remained in Natlan. He searched for his friend and then found a cave in the Secret Source Ruins, the closest place to the Night Kingdom, and slept there for several centuries. Due to the proximity of the Night Kingdom, his soul did not disappear, but when he "awoke" again, Natlan had changed. He saw that the monsters of the Abyss had returned and went to aid the Saurians, meeting the Tepetlisaurs Milray and Naiyan. After they dealt with the monsters, Antu heard Nampol's voice. This was the final battle with the Abyss, and the Ley Lines were restored, allowing the Qucusaurus's soul to return to the Night Kingdom. The whelp wanted to follow his friend, but learned that Milray had fallen ill with the same illness he had once suffered. He knew that Sacred Flame Crystals were needed to save the Tepetlisaurus, but he realized their danger. When Antu told Milray of this, the Tepetlisaurus refused to use the Crystals.

When Nampol's descendant, Ifa, learned of Milray's illness, he gathered his friends to learn more about the nature of the Tepetlisaurus's rare disease. During their study, they learned of the Bloomflower Trials, and from Milray, the Traveler learned of the harmful effects of Sacred Flame Crystals. And although they studied all the ancient scrolls and asked the Pyro Archon, nowhere was the effect of the crystals described. Milray's Saurian friends went in search of Ocean Zephyrs, while Ifa and his friends decided to obtain the Crystals. When Antu saw the Sauro-vet, he sensed something familiar about him, so he began following him and brought him to his grave, where Nampol's notes were kept. Upon learning of Antu's fate, Ifa and his friends decided to stage a scene for the Saurians in which they would first succumb to the dangerous influence of the Sacred Flame Crystals, and then everyone would be reconciled thanks to Antu. They knew the truth would change nothing for his soul, but would only reopen old wounds and sadden him once again. As a result of their performance, Antu and Milray believed the Crystals were safe again, and the Tepetlisaurus agreed to take Ifa's medicine. The Sacred Flame Crystal restored the Tepetlisaurus's strength, and it was able to play with the other Saurians and Antu. The Qucusaurus heard the voice of his friend, Nampol, again, and finally their souls were reunited in the Night Kingdom.

After learning the story of his ancestor, Ifa understood his feelings. His Qucusaurus companion, Cacucu, was different from the others, but he was as dear to him as Antu was to Nampol. One day, they were treating a sick saurian, and Cacucu became infected. He developed a fever, and Ifa did everything he could to help his friend. But Cacucu was still on the brink of death, and the Sauro-vet could only pray. If Cacucu hadn't recovered, Ifa would have felt the same guilt as his ancestor. And although Nampol began practicing medicine out of guilt, Ifa promised his ancestor that he would constantly improve his medicine so that no one else would ever have to experience that same guilt again.

customize.text: Qucusaurs

Members of Tlalocan have had a close bond with the winged Saurians, Qucusaurs, the closest to the ancient dragons Saurians, for centuries. The most striking example of this bond is the tribe's peacemaker, Chasca. Abandoned by her parents, she lived with the Qucusaurs before being adopted by Cusco. At first, she considered herself a Saurian, even though she lacked the hooked beak and sharp talons her mother, Chimpu, and elder sister, Coya, possessed. She couldn't fly, nor could she leap into the crowns of trees in a single bound. Her mother loved her just as she did her own flesh and blood, and when returning from a hunt, would always ensure her daughters ate their fill first, before contenting herself with the remainder. As Chasca grew older and learned to race across slopes and bound over rivers, she often left the nest to watch her mother and sister hunt. She memorized how they fought and adapted those techniques for her own use. She had no wings she could spread to fly, so she would leap amongst the treetops. She was not born with a beak and claw, so she would arm herself with stones in their place. During her first hunt, she attacked a foraging Forest Boar, but it knocked her to the ground. Chasca returned empty-handed, her whole body ragged, covered head to toe in injuries and abrasions, so Coya vigorously opposed any future forays. Once the girl recovered, she again set out into the mountains, collecting sharp-edged stones, sticks, sticky sap, and animal skins. From what she found, she fashioned a slingshot to fire stones, and finally became able to hunt animals. Over time, Chasca mastered new fighting techniques, as if there was always some voice in the dark guiding her on, and she became obsessed with battle. Chasca's mother realized she could not overcome this "illness," so she gave her daughter to humans, but continued to love her.

Not all Qucusaurs are friendly to humans, and Chasca's older sister, Coya, was one of them. When Chimpu gave Chasca to humans, Coya strongly protested and became even less willing to interact with humans. At first, the sisters remained best friends, and Chasca would always escape to her during troubles in the tribe, but then the girl increasingly tried to understand human behavior and spent more time with them. When it was Coya's turn to leave the nest, she suggested that her sister leave the tribe and go live with her. Chasca was torn: on the one hand, she had decided to become part of a new family and embrace her human nature, but on the other, she didn't want to make Coya unhappy. Coya took this hesitation as a response and considered it a betrayal, causing a huge scandal. They didn't see each other for many years after that, until Chasca's sister ran into trouble. A group of humans manufacturing phlogiston wings abducted Coya's daughter, Chime, and the Saurian began attacking the phlogiston wing traders in an attempt to find her daughter. With the help of the Traveler and Paimon, Chasca set out to rescue her niece from captivity in a flying laboratory. During a clash with Elder Allpa and her supporters, the unstable relic from Ochkanatlan powering the laboratory was damaged and threatened to explode. Chasca carried the relic away from the laboratory and the tribe, and Coya shielded her from the blast. Despite their past differences, Coya understood why her sister chose to remain among humans and accepted her choice.

The tribe's main Sauro-vet, Ifa, is accompanied by an unusual Qucusaurus named Cacucu. Ifa always believed he couldn't sympathize with and shelter every wounded Saurian he encountered, lest he abandon his clinic and live in the wild. The self-discipline he'd demonstrated over the years was commendable, but meeting Cacucu changed everything. When Ifa first saw him, the young Saurian was being beaten by other Saurians because he looked different. He was covered in blood, and his life was on the line, so Ifa took him under his wing for a while. Although the Sauro-vet didn't remember it, he had met Cacucu before. The Qucusaurus's mother had once been seriously injured, and if not for Ifa's prompt intervention, she might not have laid an egg with Cacucu. And the first thing the Saurian saw was Ifa. The Qucusaurus's mother eventually died from her old injuries, and the little sick whelp couldn't survive alone, so he concluded that Ifa, who had helped his mother, was the most suitable candidate to take over her role. And if he could one day become an assistant at the clinic and repay Ifa for his service, it would be a remarkable feat. Ifa's best friend, Ororon of the Masters of the Night-Wind, also played a role in turning "for a while" into "forever." He pointed at the vegetables in his field sporting prominent Cacucu-beak-shaped holes in their leaves, and the vet was forced to take the Qucusaurus in. In fact, Cacucu was a smart Saurian and understood that he had to corner Ifa to get into his clinic. Cacucu eventually became the vet's assistant at the clinic and often helps him with patients. Since the Qucusaurus has the unique ability not only to understand human speech but also to speak a few phrases in it, it often translates the words of wounded Saurians for Ifa. And Ifa, in turn, uses her Vision to take Cacucu, who never grew up, with him on flights.

Cacucu's curiosity and ability to speak sometimes lead to unexpected consequences. One day, Ifa's friend, Ororon, went to Fontaine for the opening of the Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland amusement park to deliver fresh vegetables from Natlan. It was his first time traveling so far from home, so the elders of the Masters of the Night-Wind sent Ifa along with him. But in Fontaine, Ifa and Cacucu encountered a law prohibiting flying objects on certain days of the month. When guards began pursuing them, Cacucu flew into the nearest building, which turned out to be the Palais Mermonia, the main building of Fontaine, where Chief Justice Neuvillette resides, as well as the main chambers of the nation. When the Traveler and Paimon, who knew the Chief Justice, went to help the Qucusaurus, they overheard a conversation in his office between the Iudex himself, Wriothesley, the manager of the Fortress of Meropide, and Cacucu. The Traveler and Paimon told them about the Saurian, but since time was needed to determine whether he was a flying object and to sign a non-disclosure agreement, as Cacucu had overheard a conversation about smuggling, the Qucusaurus remained with Neuvillette. During Cacucu's time at the Palais Mermonia, Wriothesley managed to teach him a new phrase and began considering getting a pet, while Neuvillette, who could be considered a distant relative of the Saurians as being the Hydro Dragon, learned to understand the Qucusaurus.

contents.text: ~2,000 years ago
The Eighth Lord, "Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers" Ix Ajkotz'i'j Iq'ismal Waxak, ruled the territory of the future clan and adopted the human girl Lianca.
Lianca, who would later receive the Ancient Name Vuka, was joined by refugees and founded the Flower-Feather Clan.
Lianca joined Xbalanque in the war against the dragons.
Xbalanque became the Pyro Archon and ruler of the Grand Alliance, and Lianca became the clan's First Speaker.
Och-Kan became ruler of the Grand Alliance.
Lianca's son betrayed his mother and offered Och-Kan to kill the First Speaker, but Lianca killed her son and the tyrant's warriors, dying in battle.
Lianca's daughter, who defeated the dragon, became the clan's Speaker. An Alliance officer, on Och-Kan's orders, wanted to marry the Speaker and take over the clan, but she burned them both.
The tribe's elder exiled the scarlet-eyed youth, who led a rebellion against Och-Kan.
After Och-Kan's overthrow, the scarlet-eyed youth became the second Pyro Archon and ordered his name erased from history.
~500 years ago
The hero of Natlan, Menilek, who bore the Ancient Name Vuka, set out on a pilgrimage with his Qucusaurus companion, Ngoubou.
Menilek joined the exiled Tenoch in the war against the Abyss, without completing the pilgrimage.
Menilek died during the battle.
Ngoubou became the Goldflame Qucusaur Tyrant.
Ten years after the Cataclysm, the warrior Taika gathered a group, including the warrior Quenin, to pursue the Jade of Return.
Taika and Quenin died in Ochkanatlan.
Taika's daughter, Bona, set out for Ochkanatlan for the Jade of Return, but also died.
The final Bloomflower Trials were held, turning into a battle between the tribes.
Present Day
Mutota became the tribe's leader.
Chasca, one of the future six heroes of Natlan, who bears the Ancient Name Vuka, was born.
Chasca was abandoned by her parents and adopted by the Qucusaurs.
Due to the Abyssal infestation, Chasca was given to humans and later became a Peacemaker.
Elder Allpa's son, Tepal, built a sky laboratory to create phlogiston wings.
Tepal died during experiments.
The Abyss launched a full-scale invasion of Natlan.
Chasca's sister, Chuychu, died in the war with the Abyss.
The Pyro Archon used the power of the six heroes of Natlan, the Ruler of Death, and the divine throne to drive back the Abyss.
The Abyss was destroyed.
Allpa kidnaps the Qucusaurs to use them to create phlogiston wings.
The sky laboratory was converted into a prison, where Allpa is imprisoned.
The next Bloomflower Trials were being conducted to save a saurian.
